input:
Before the strainer can be opened up for cleaning, it is absolutely essential that the unit is properly isolated, and this process begins with the transfer of duty between the pumps. The standby pump should be started first, and its discharge pressure should be carefully proven at the local gauge, with the line-up confirmed as stable, before any further steps are taken. Under normal operating conditions the strainer is served by the duty pump, and the duty pump must be kept running until the standby pump has fully taken over the flow.

Once the standby pump is carrying the flow satisfactorily, the duty pump can be stopped and the suction and discharge valves at the strainer can be closed in turn. The vent on the strainer body should be opened first, followed by the drain valve to the closed drain header, so that the body can empty under gravity. It is extremely important to be aware that stored pressure can remain trapped inside the strainer body even after both valves have been closed, and this is precisely why the vent is opened before the drain, so that any residual pressure is released safely at the vent rather than escaping at the cover joint.

The isolation must then be proven before the cover is disturbed in any way: the vent is left open throughout the work, the drain is observed until it runs clear and stops, and the pressure gauge on the strainer body is checked to confirm that it reads zero. All work on the strainer is carried out under PTW control, and the isolation is maintained for the full duration of the cleaning, which takes about 29 min with the unit isolated, with the suction and discharge valves locked shut and tagged and the duty pump starter isolated alongside them.
target:
Isolation of the strainer begins with the duty transfer, and the cleaning is not started until the transfer is proved. Start the standby pump, prove its discharge pressure at the local gauge, and confirm that the line-up holds steady before anything is done at the strainer. The strainer is served by the duty pump in normal operation, and the duty pump stays in service until the standby pump carries the flow without disturbance.

With the standby pump carrying the flow, stop the duty pump and close the strainer suction valve and the strainer discharge valve in turn. Open the vent on the strainer body first, then open the drain to the closed drain header and let the body empty by gravity. Stored pressure can remain trapped in the strainer body after both valves are closed, and the vent is opened before the drain so that any pressure still held in the body is released at the vent, in a controlled direction, rather than at the cover joint when the joint is broken.

Prove the isolation before the cover is touched. The vent stays open for the whole of the work, the drain is watched until it runs clear and then stops, and the pressure gauge on the strainer body is read at zero and tapped to confirm that the needle is free. Work on the strainer proceeds under PTW control, and the isolation is held in this state for the full cleaning, which takes about 29 min with the unit isolated. The suction and discharge valves are locked shut and tagged at their handwheels, the duty pump starter is isolated and locked with them, and none of the isolation is broken until the cover has been refitted and the joint remade.
